set_aside.subject: Bootstrap success output
set_aside.text: the success message shows the normalized email to the operator who supplied it
set_aside.question: Through which output channel and in what stable form must the bootstrap command expose the normalized email, and may any other success data be printed?
options: Print a human-readable message containing the normalized email on stdout
Print it on stderr while reserving stdout for machine-readable output
Return only the documented exit code to scripts and show the email through an explicitly interactive terminal channel
set_aside.default_guess: Print one human-readable success line containing the normalized email on stdout and no password or other account data.

witness.initial: A deployment has no staff account, and an operator invokes the bootstrap command from a wrapper that captures stdout and stderr separately.
events: The operator supplies an email whose normalized form differs from the supplied spelling and a password.
The command creates the administrator successfully.
outcomes: One implementation writes the normalized email to stdout, so the wrapper captures it as ordinary command output.
Another writes it to stderr or directly to the terminal, so the wrapper's stdout contains no email.
witness.observer: The host operator and deployment wrapper see different output contracts.

set_aside.subject: Viewer-entry rate limiting
set_aside.text: entry is rate limited, not origin-checked
set_aside.question: What identifies a rate-limit bucket, what limit and time window apply, when is the bucket consumed, and what observable failure is returned when the limit is reached?
options: Limit by both source IP and credential fingerprint, with separate or combined quotas
set_aside.default_guess: Use bounded per-IP and per-credential-fingerprint counters, consume an attempt before credential verification, and return the same concealed entry failure once limited.

witness.initial: A valid viewer access link exists and two users share one public IP address.
events: An attacker submits repeated invalid access links from that IP.
The legitimate viewer then submits the valid link from the same IP.
outcomes: An IP-based limiter refuses the legitimate viewer because the shared bucket is exhausted.
A credential-based limiter accepts the legitimate viewer because attempts using other credentials did not consume its bucket.
witness.observer: The legitimate viewer sees whether entry succeeds.

set_aside.subject: Viewer sign-out origin enforcement
set_aside.text: a viewer sign-out is refused unless it comes from the portal's own public origin
set_aside.question: Which request evidence establishes that a sign-out came from the public origin, which configured origin is authoritative if more than one trusted origin exists, and how are missing or `null` origin evidence handled?
options: Require an exact `Origin` header match to one designated public origin and reject missing or `null` values
Use `Origin` when present and a `Referer` or host-based fallback when it is absent
set_aside.default_guess: Require an exact `Origin` header match to a single configured public origin and reject missing, `null`, or differently configured origins.

witness.initial: A viewer has a valid same-site-strict session cookie, and the deployment has two configured trusted origins.
events: The browser sends a sign-out request carrying the cookie and an `Origin` matching the secondary trusted origin.
outcomes: One implementation accepts the request because every configured trusted origin counts as the portal's own origin.
Another refuses it because only the designated public origin qualifies.
witness.observer: The viewer sees whether the session is ended.

set_aside.subject: Implicit manual budget created by progress read
set_aside.text: a staff read of a project's progress list, when the project has no manual budget version yet, creates that empty manual budget version
set_aside.question: Is the newly created empty manual budget version active, inactive, or conditionally active, especially when an imported snapshot is already active?
options: Make it active only when the project has no active budget version
Make it the active budget even if another source was active
set_aside.default_guess: Create it inactive; a read must not silently change the active budget source or replace an active imported snapshot.

witness.initial: An archived project has an active approved-estimate snapshot and no manual budget version.
events: An authorized staff member reads the project's progress list.
The read creates the promised empty manual budget version.
A viewer subsequently reads the project's budget summary.
outcomes: If the new manual version is inactive, the viewer still sees the approved snapshot as the active budget.
If it becomes active, the viewer sees an empty manual budget or a changed budget source.
witness.observer: The viewer and staff member see different active-budget state.

set_aside.subject: Authorization of progress-read side effect
set_aside.text: a staff read of a project's progress list, when the project has no manual budget version yet, creates that empty manual budget version
set_aside.question: Does authorization for reading progress also authorize the budget-creation side effect, or must the caller additionally hold a budget-mutation capability?
options: The progress-read capability alone authorizes the exceptional creation
Both progress-read and manual-budget-mutation capabilities are required
The read succeeds without creation when the caller lacks budget-mutation capability
set_aside.default_guess: Treat the exceptional creation as part of the progress-read operation and require only the capability normally required to read that progress list.

witness.initial: An active staff account is assigned to an archived project and may read its progress, but its capability set does not include maintaining manual budgets; the project has no manual budget version.
events: The staff member requests the progress list.
outcomes: One implementation returns the list and creates the empty manual budget because the read permission carries the side effect.
Another refuses the request or returns it without creating the budget because budget mutation requires an additional capability.
witness.observer: The staff member sees a different response, and later staff see different stored budget state.

set_aside.subject: Failure atomicity of progress read and implicit budget creation
set_aside.text: a staff read of a project's progress list, when the project has no manual budget version yet, creates that empty manual budget version
set_aside.question: Must creation of the empty manual budget and production of the progress-list response be atomic, and what happens if either the creation or the subsequent read fails?
options: Commit both effects as one transaction or leave neither effect
Allow the budget to remain created even when the progress-list request ultimately fails
Return the progress list even if creation fails, leaving the project without a manual budget
set_aside.default_guess: Make creation and the progress-list read one atomic operation: failure returns an explicit storage-unavailable response and leaves no newly created budget.

witness.initial: An archived project has no manual budget version, and an authorized staff member requests its progress list.
events: The service successfully inserts the empty manual budget.
A storage error occurs while completing the progress query or response.
outcomes: A transactional implementation rolls back the budget and returns failure.
A non-transactional implementation returns failure but leaves the empty manual budget stored.
witness.observer: The requesting staff member sees the failure, and a later staff read or budget query sees whether the budget was left behind.
